Findings:
- The pinned snapshot (project d8d46c95, Mathlib 25730c7c, SimonGMT 2b366308 per lake-manifest and package HEADs) contains the frozen Ch06 contract, byte-identical to the workspace Submission.
- SimonGMT defines covectorEuclideanNorm as √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} if StrictMono I then α(basisFun ∘ I)² else 0) (Mass.lean:30), with Covector E n = E [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ (Forms.lean:31).
- SimonGMT has no orthonormal-basis invariance, counting identity or wedge-norm bound for this norm. Its only wedge estimate (norm_covectorWedge_le) is for the operator norm, and it contains no OrthonormalBasis usage in Chapter06.
- Mathlib provides the needed tools: OrthonormalBasis.norm_dual (‖L‖² = Σ L(b_i)², the one-slot Parseval step), Orthonormal.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension_of_card_eq, InnerProductSpace.toDual_symm_apply, alternatizeUncurryFin_apply, curryLeft_apply_apply, ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply, map_eq_zero_of_not_injective, AlternatingMap.map_perm and the Tuple.sort API.
- Mathlib's exterior-power bilinear forms act on ⋀[R]^n M, not on continuous alternating maps, and provide no coefficient-norm invariance. So all five children are new obligations.
- In the replayed comparator child scope, all five child types and the parent type elaborate. The StrictMono decidability instance matches the one in covectorEuclideanNorm's definition.
- The parent follows from the children with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. Scratch proofs of all five children compile with the same axioms.
- No proposed name occurs in the snapshot project or among the 217 DAG nodes.
- Simon 1.5–1.6 (local book) states that the covector inner product is induced from ℝ^P, which supports the basis independence in Step 3.

subproblem.title: Orthonormal basis adapted to a linear functional: α(u_0) = ‖α‖ and α(u_j) = 0 for j ≠ 0 (parent Steps 4–5)
subproblem.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ and every continuous linear functional α : ℝ^P → ℝ (Eucl P →L[ℝ] ℝ) there is an orthonormal basis u = (u_0,…,u_{P−1}) of ℝ^P, indexed by Fin P, such that for every j ∈ Fin P: α(u_j) = ‖α‖ (the operator norm) if j = 0, and α(u_j) = 0 if j ≠ 0. No hypothesis α ≠ 0 is needed: for α = 0 the standard basis works.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (α : Eucl P →L[ℝ] ℝ), ∃ u : OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ (Eucl P), ∀ j : Fin P, α (u j) = if (j : ℕ) = 0 then ‖α‖ else 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Steps 4–5 (the trivial case α = 0 and the adapted orthonormal basis).

Claim. For every P and every continuous linear functional α : ℝ^P → ℝ, there is an orthonormal basis u = (u_0,…,u_{P−1}) of ℝ^P indexed by [P] := {0,…,P−1} such that, for every j ∈ [P], α(u_j) = ‖α‖ if j = 0 and α(u_j) = 0 if j ≠ 0. Here ‖α‖ is the operator norm.

1. (Case α = 0.) Then ‖α‖ = 0. Take u := e, the standard basis, which is orthonormal. For every j, α(e_j) = 0; this equals ‖α‖ = 0 if j = 0 and equals 0 if j ≠ 0. This case includes P = 0, where [P] is empty and the condition is vacuous.

2. (Case α ≠ 0: Riesz vector.) By the Riesz representation on ℝ^P there is a ∈ ℝ^P with α(z) = ⟨a, z⟩ for all z; namely a := (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ ℝ^P)⁻¹ α. Moreover |a| = ‖α‖. By Cauchy–Schwarz, |α(z)| ≤ |a||z| for all z, so ‖α‖ ≤ |a|. Also |a|² = α(a) ≤ ‖α‖|a|, so |a| ≤ ‖α‖ (trivial if a = 0). Equivalently, the Riesz map is a linear isometry. Since α ≠ 0, a ≠ 0, so |a| > 0.

3. (P ≥ 1.) ℝ^0 = {0}, so the existence of a ≠ 0 forces P ≥ 1. Hence 0 ∈ [P].

4. (Extension to an orthonormal basis.) v := a/|a| satisfies |v| = 1, so the one-member family (v), indexed by {0} ⊆ [P], is orthonormal. Since dim ℝ^P = P = #[P], this family extends to an orthonormal basis u of ℝ^P indexed by [P] with u_0 = v. This is Gram–Schmidt; in Mathlib, apply Orthonormal.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension_of_card_eq to s := {0} and the constant family j ↦ v, using finrank ℝ ℝ^P = P = Fintype.card (Fin P).

5. (Values.) α(u_0) = ⟨a, a/|a|⟩ = |a|²/|a| = |a| = ‖α‖. For j ≠ 0 we have a = |a|·u_0, hence α(u_j) = ⟨a, u_j⟩ = |a|·⟨u_0, u_j⟩ = 0, because u is orthonormal and u_0 ⊥ u_j for j ≠ 0.

6. (Conclusion.) In both cases α(u_j) = (‖α‖ if j = 0, else 0) for all j ∈ [P]. ∎

Formalization pointers: InnerProductSpace.toDual_symm_apply (⟨(toDual ℝ E).symm α, x⟩ = α x), and the isometry property of toDual for |a| = ‖α‖. Orthonormal.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension_of_card_eq takes hv : Orthonormal ℝ (s.domRestrict v). Use OrthonormalBasis.orthonormal for ⟨u_0, u_j⟩ = 0. In case 1, EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ works.
proof_key_steps: α = 0: ‖α‖ = 0, and the standard basis satisfies the condition.
α ≠ 0: there is a Riesz vector a with α = ⟨a,·⟩ and |a| = ‖α‖ > 0; in particular P ≥ 1.
Extend the unit vector a/|a|, placed at index 0, to an orthonormal basis u of ℝ^P (dim ℝ^P = P).

audit.reason: The zero-functional case includes P = 0. Otherwise the Riesz vector forces P > 0; extending its normalization at index zero and applying orthogonality gives all required values. The natural-number index test in Lean correctly expresses the prose without requiring an inhabitant of Fin 0. No hypothesis is missing.
